key_insight: OmniVideo-100K introduces a large-scale dataset designed to improve audio-visual reasoning by preserving the link between sounds, visuals, and structured evidence. Instead of treating audio and video separately, it encourages models to reason through coherent scripts and evidence chains across the whole video.
problem_solved: The paper addresses a key weakness in current video QA pipelines: they often split videos into short clips and generate separate audio and visual captions, which breaks the relationship between modalities and leads to inconsistent descriptions. It also tackles the challenge of long-form audio-visual understanding for more reliable QA.
method: Builds a dataset of 100K audio-visual examples centered on structured scripts and evidence chains.
Supports reasoning that connects audio cues to their visual sources rather than processing them independently.
Provides a training/evaluation resource aimed at improving consistency across clips and better long-context video comprehension.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this dataset can help train models that reason more faithfully over multimodal video content and reduce hallucinations from disconnected captioning. It is especially useful for researchers working on video QA, multimodal reasoning, and long-video understanding.
